scope: Completion audit of the15top-level product goals L6–L20. It supplements, and does not replace, the complete838-entry ledger or detailed acceptance requirements. File inspection and existing run artifacts are supporting evidence, not new runtime tests.

rows.requirement: * Pair two laptops in seconds with minimal user interaction.
rows.evidence: Single-host pairing and readiness tests pass in the current native headless suites.
rows.missing: Two actual laptops, discovery reliability and observed pairing time across home Wi-Fi, hotspot and mixed interfaces.

rows.requirement: * Support single files, multiple files, folders, and very large files.
rows.evidence: Current tests exercise selected files, mixed dropped items, folders and exact boundaries. A predecessor 5 GiB transfer/save and current modeled high-address reads provide separate limited evidence.
rows.missing: Current-build native source/destination large transfers and the full requested size/tree/platform matrix.

rows.requirement: * Transfer directly over the local network at the highest practical Wi-Fi/LAN speed.
rows.evidence: The predecessor 5 GiB payload interval measured 15.41 MB/s; its matched 1 GiB control measured 15.92 MB/s on one host with synthetic source data.
rows.missing: Actual LAN/Wi-Fi and disk baselines, target-device repetitions and justified highest-practical-throughput acceptance. The earlier 44.56 MB/s discrepancy remains unexplained.

rows.requirement: * Keep memory usage bounded even for 10 GB, 50 GB, 100 GB+ transfers.
rows.evidence: Predecessor 5 GiB transfer/save has complete timed process samples. Diagnostic audit allocation is distinguished from production receive, verify and save phases.
rows.missing: Actual 10/50/100 GB+ memory/resource observations on target devices. Address models allocate only selected small ranges and do not prove memory scaling.

rows.requirement: * Resume interrupted transfers instead of restarting them.
rows.evidence: Current unit and single-host browser cases recover durable blocks and verify exact output after reload/crash/journal faults.
rows.missing: Physical interruption/resume across required networks, devices and representative large trees.

rows.requirement: * Recover cleanly from Wi-Fi drops, refreshes, sleep/wake, crashes, and reconnects.
rows.evidence: Current suites cover peer interruption, refresh, renderer/browser process termination and source recovery under controlled faults.
rows.missing: Real Wi-Fi loss, laptop sleep/wake and hardware/browser/OS recovery matrix. Scripted faults do not reproduce all physical failure modes.

rows.requirement: * Verify transferred data using cryptographic hashes so corrupted files can never be reported as successfully transferred.
rows.evidence: Current code authenticates block routing fields and payload, verifies final stream and destination bytes, and tests corruption without success labels.
rows.missing: The full fault/corruption/native filesystem matrix and target-device observations. Selected tests do not prove the absolute claim for every possible fault.

rows.requirement: * Make pairing secure enough that files cannot accidentally be sent to the wrong device.
rows.evidence: Authorization and preparation-privacy tests exercise matching codes and two-sided consent before source metadata/payload disclosure.
rows.missing: Real wrong-device/human-code comparison and final adversarial/security review across the required deployment environment.

rows.requirement: * Hide WebRTC, ports, networking, SDP, OPFS, and other technical concepts from normal users.
rows.evidence: Primary views use send/receive actions and an Other transfer methods section; recovery tests exercise advice with raw diagnostics behind details.
rows.missing: Independent nontechnical-user review of all relevant states and errors on actual devices. Source inspection and scripted text assertions do not establish user comprehension.

rows.requirement: * Provide a simple UX: **Send → Select Files → Pair → Transfer → Verified Complete**.
rows.evidence: Current single-host tests cover selecting, pairing, consent, transfer verification and saving; core UI exposes the primary send/receive flow.
rows.missing: Unassisted end-to-end use and observed discoverability/timing with nontechnical users on the real laptop pair.

rows.requirement: * Show accurate transfer speed, progress, ETA, transferred size, and connection status.
rows.evidence: Rate-window tests distinguish current/recent rates, exclude resumed bytes and handle stalls/resets. Current browser cases cover durable byte totals, elapsed time, pause, verification and interrupted-state displays. Receiver reconnect resets progress before a new attempt.
rows.missing: Target-device accuracy/ETA observations under variable real network/disk rates and long transfers. No new elapsed-time bug was established in this audit.

rows.requirement: * Require no internet or cloud storage for local transfers.
rows.evidence: Both peer constructors configure empty ICE-server lists; the packaged runtime, rendezvous and assets are local. Existing native single-host tests do not require a cloud transfer service.
rows.missing: Actual two-laptop operation with internet unavailable and environment/network observations. This audit does not certify unrelated browser or OS background traffic.

rows.requirement: * Avoid forcing users to reselect or rehash huge files when only the connection fails.
rows.evidence: Current preparation/retry tests retain pending or completed source preparation without another read/hash solely for connection retry; changed-source recovery is refused.
rows.missing: Representative native very-large-file retries and physical permission/restart/network scenarios.

rows.requirement: * Handle thousands of files and multi-gigabyte transfers without freezes, crashes, corrupted state, or excessive disk/network overhead.
rows.evidence: Current save-recovery tests construct 1,200-file trees and verify output/reuse after interruption. The predecessor multi-GiB measurements have their stated synthetic-source scope.
rows.missing: Full mixed-tree/size/resource/performance matrix on target devices, including freezes and disk/network overhead under real load.

rows.requirement: * Provide clear recovery actions whenever something goes wrong.
rows.evidence: Current error/advice tests cover unavailable services, quota failures, corrupted-copy discard, interrupted transfers and retry actions; raw details are expandable.
rows.missing: All listed failure modes plus independent usability validation on the physical setup. Controlled tested recovery paths are partial evidence.

remainingEnvironmentGates: Actual two-laptop network/sleep/wake/native source/destination and nontechnical-usability validation.
Native default-handler/picker GUI, clean OS and hosted final-revision CI.
Requested real large-size resource/throughput matrix; prior5GiB observations and selected50/100GiB address models cannot substitute.
